title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election in California's 3rd Congressional District
description: This race will determine who represents California's newly redrawn 3rd Congressional District following the passage of Proposition 50 in 2025. The district now covers Nevada County, El Dorado County, and parts of Placer and Sacramento counties, shifting from a Republican-leaning seat to one that Democrat Kamala Harris won by 10 points in 2024. Incumbent Republican Kevin Kiley opted to run in the 6th District, leaving the seat open. The general election pits Democratic U.S. Rep. Ami Bera, a physician who has served in Congress since 2013, against Republican Robb Tucker, a Nevada County Supervisor and small business owner.
polling_note: No general election opinion polls were found for this race. The Cook Political Report rates the district as D+6 (Solid Democratic) as of November 2025.

candidates.name: Ami Bera
candidates.summary: Ami Bera is a physician and Democratic U.S. Representative first elected in 2012, currently representing California's 6th Congressional District. He serves on the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence. He is running in the newly redrawn 3rd District after redistricting.

candidates.name: Robb Tucker
candidates.summary: Robb Tucker is a Nevada County Supervisor (District 2) who was elected in 2024 and took office in January 2025. A lifelong Nevada County resident, he previously served as President/CEO of his family's mobilehome community business until 2020. He is running for Congress on a platform of public safety, limited regulation, and local economic development.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast relies on structural and contextual signals. The newly redrawn 3rd District covers parts of Nevada, El Dorado, Placer, and Sacramento counties and is described as shifting from a Republican-leaning seat to one Kamala Harris carried by 10 points in 2024. Cook Political Report rates it D+6 (Solid Democratic). The seat is open because incumbent Republican Kevin Kiley is running in the 6th District, removing any GOP incumbency advantage. Democratic nominee Ami Bera is a long-serving U.S. Representative (since 2013) with institutional advantages in fundraising and name recognition, while Republican Robb Tucker is a first-term Nevada County Supervisor with a more limited electoral profile. The Democratic lean of the district and quality of the Democratic nominee point to a clear but not overwhelming advantage. The absence of district-specific polling, the fact that this is a newly configured district, and the possibility that local GOP strength in some portions (e.g., Placer County) could produce a closer-than-expected race keep confidence at medium rather than high.
